taskVersion.name: ves-synthetic-a-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station T-15, survey area T. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1132.2 | 7.42 | 7.42
2 | 3621.5 | 17.67 | 25.09
3 | 4447.9 | 1.70 | 26.79
4 | 4307.5 | 0.53 | 27.32
5 | 7664.9 | 4.92 | 32.24
6 | 12762.9 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as HKHA-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station T-15, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Note – Station T-15, Survey Area T**

The VES model at T-15 comprises six layers with resistivities increasing overall from 1132.2 Ω·m at the surface to 12762.9 Ω·m at depth, interrupted by a minor resistivity dip between layers 3 and 4 (4447.9 → 4307.5 Ω·m) before rising again to 7664.9 and 12762.9 Ω·m in layers 5 and 6.

Applying the standard triplet rule to the resistivity sequence gives:
- Layers 1-2-3: increasing → A
- Layers 2-3-4: rise then fall → K
- Layers 3-4-5: fall then rise → H
- Layers 4-5-6: increasing → A

This yields a curve type of **AKHA**, not the **HKHA** type recorded in the file. The first segment (layers 1-2-3) is strictly increasing (A), not H as filed. The discrepancy should be corrected in the station record before further use in cross-sections or layer correlation.

{"curve_type_stated": "AKHA", "label_issue_flagged": true}
